name: 67-unicode
note: The page does not name its character set. wkhtmltopdf assumes an old Western one, so every Greek, Cyrillic and accented letter, maths sign and curly quote comes out garbled (Î±Î²Î³ for αβγ, cafÃ© for café); marqius-wkhtmltopdf prints them as written. Name the character set in the page, or pass --encoding utf-8, and both agree (options/encoding).

name: 70-visibility
note: wkhtmltopdf turns the half-transparent line into a low-resolution picture (96 dots an inch), so it prints blurred and its words cannot be searched or copied; marqius-wkhtmltopdf keeps them as sharp text. The rest of the page is the same.

name: 61-svg-inline
note: The pages look the same: both paint the gradient red to blue, wkhtmltopdf as a picture and marqius-wkhtmltopdf as a gradient, and both set the label in Arial. Compare's picture of this page shows marqius-wkhtmltopdf's box flat grey because compare does not draw gradients.

name: 69-borders
note: wkhtmltopdf draws the rounded box as a picture, marqius-wkhtmltopdf as shapes. The pages look the same.

name: 71-forms
note: Form fields: wkhtmltopdf draws the drop-down arrow as a picture, which marqius-wkhtmltopdf leaves out; a ticked box shows a filled square where wkhtmltopdf draws a tick; marqius-wkhtmltopdf sets the Send button's label at 7.8 pt where wkhtmltopdf uses 9.6 pt; and the lines under the fields sit up to 2.4 pt higher.

name: 42-inline-format
note: The first line's words stand up to 1.4 pt along the line from where wkhtmltopdf puts them (subscript and superscript). The pages look the same.

name: certificate
note: wkhtmltopdf writes the letter-spaced title as single letters (it reads back as C E RT IFIC AT E); marqius-wkhtmltopdf keeps the word whole. The pages look the same.

name: statement
note: The pages look the same. The customer's name block is read back in another order, which the text measure counts.

name: javascript
note: The page builds its invoice table with a script (getElementById, createElement). marqius-wkhtmltopdf runs it with the page's DOM, as wkhtmltopdf does, and the pages look the same.

name: no-charset
note: An invoice that does not name its character set: wkhtmltopdf garbles every accented letter and the euro sign (SociÃ©tÃ© for Société, â‚¬ for €); marqius-wkhtmltopdf prints them as written. With --encoding utf-8 both agree (options/encoding).

name: a5-portrait
note: Uses report.html (12 px Arial, line-height 1.45) on A5 paper. Page 1 matches line for line, but wkhtmltopdf moves the table's "Midlands" row to page 2 where marqius-wkhtmltopdf still fits it at the foot of page 1, so page 2 starts a row later and its lines sit 17.4 pt higher.

name: zoom
note: Uses report.html at --zoom 1.25. marqius-wkhtmltopdf scales text a little differently: the 21 pt title comes out 20.7 pt, and words stand up to 3.5 pt along their lines from where wkhtmltopdf puts them; the page breaks are the same.

name: landscape-letter
note: The table's columns stand 1 to 2 pt further right. The pages look the same.

name: long-statement
note: The amounts stand 1.2 pt further right. The pages look the same.

name: print-media
note: In the order table, marqius-wkhtmltopdf wraps "12 × A4 copier paper" onto two lines; wkhtmltopdf keeps it on one.

name: notice-he
note: The pages look the same. Copied or searched, marqius-wkhtmltopdf's text gives back 43 of the notice's 48 words as written, wkhtmltopdf's 28: it splits many Hebrew words into single letters, which is the text measure's loss.

name: invoice-ar
note: The pages look the same. Copied or searched, marqius-wkhtmltopdf's text gives back 48 of the invoice's 56 words as written, wkhtmltopdf's 2: it stores the Arabic as separate letter shapes, which is most of the text measure's loss.

name: letter-hi
note: Both pages look alike. marqius-wkhtmltopdf's text reads back as clean Hindi; wkhtmltopdf's does not (16 of its letters have no text at all), which is most of the text measure's loss. Letters joined with र (ra), as in प्रिय and ग्राहक, come out apart, with the halant showing, where wkhtmltopdf joins them.

name: letter-hi
note: The pages look the same, but for two quantities and the total in the table, which stand 1.2 to 1.5 pt further right. Copied or searched, marqius-wkhtmltopdf's text reads back as clean Hindi; wkhtmltopdf's does not (16 of its letters have no text at all), which is most of the text measure's loss.

name: receipt-th
note: The pages look the same. Copied or searched, marqius-wkhtmltopdf's text comes back as clean Thai; wkhtmltopdf's has its tone and vowel marks split off.

name: invoice-zh
note: The pages look the same, but wkhtmltopdf's text has look-alike signs in place of some characters, so a search for the company's name in its PDF finds nothing; marqius-wkhtmltopdf's has the real characters.

name: letter-ja
note: The pages look the same. wkhtmltopdf sets the text in Noto Sans Mono CJK HK, marqius-wkhtmltopdf in Noto Sans CJK JP, the face lang="ja" asks for; wkhtmltopdf's text reads back with some characters as radicals.

name: mixed-scripts
note: The pages look the same. wkhtmltopdf sets all the Chinese, Japanese and Korean words in Noto Sans CJK HK, marqius-wkhtmltopdf in Noto Sans CJK JP.

name: receipt-ko
note: The pages look the same. The wide space after the time reads back as a different space character in the two PDFs.

name: script-file
note: A real difference: marqius-wkhtmltopdf runs scripts written in the page, but not one the page loads from a file (<script src>), so the delivery note's number, lines and parcel count, which script-file.js writes, are missing.
